chunks: And from him from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara from Humran who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Indeed, in the book of Ali (peace be upon him): When they pray Friday in its time, then pray with them.'
Zurara said: I said to him, 'This is what, if you feared, I would not follow him as an Imam.'

Humran said: 'How can I fear you, while I did not ask him? He is the one who initiated it, and said: In the book of Ali (peace be upon him): When they pray Friday in its time, then pray with them.' How is there in this from him any fear (taqiyya)?'
I said: 'You have feared, and this is what is not permissible until it was decreed that we gathered at the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).'

Humran said to him: 'May Allah improve you, I narrated to you this hadith which you narrated to me: 'Indeed in the book of Ali (peace be upon him): When they pray Friday in its time, then pray with them.''
He said: 'This is when the enemy of Allah is a sinner (fasiq), it is not fitting for us to follow him nor to pray with him.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'In the book of Ali (peace be upon him): When they pray Friday in its time, then pray with them.' And do not rise from your place until you pray two additional rak'ahs.'
I said: 'So I would have prayed four for myself, not following him.' He said: 'Yes.'
He said: So he was silent, and my companion was silent, and we were pleased.

key_terms.اِتَّقَاكَ: You feared (referring to taqiyya or fear of following)
key_terms.تَقِيَّةٌ: Fear/Precaution (often used in context of hiding belief or cautious action)
key_terms.فَاسِقٌ: Sinner (one who commits sins but remains Muslim)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying behind a sinful Imam according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the Shia jurisprudential distinction between praying in congregation behind a *fasiq* (sinner) and fully emulating him as a valid Imam, a key topic in Usul al-Fiqh regarding the validity of Salah. Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that while one prays with them, the prayer is not fully attributed to their leadership, instructing the follower to pray two additional rak'ahs to ensure the prayer is complete and independent of the Imam's potential deficiency. This ruling underscores the Shia principle that the piety of the Imam affects the perfection of the congregational prayer but not necessarily its fundamental validity.
